title: Atlas R2.0 Windows debug runtime discovery v4
description: Closed structural schema for four incomplete, non-authoritative Windows DEBUG_PROCESS discovery artifacts adding borrowed debug-event file-handle identity and stable same-handle whole-file on-disk reads to the v3 target-only reconciliation lane.
$comment: The file-identity trace binds only non-null borrowed debug-event image hFile values to FILE_ID_INFO and two equal same-handle whole-file on-disk reads while the debuggee is suspended. Those bytes are not mapped or loaded memory bytes. Target-only K32 endpoint reconciliation remains checked against received debug-image events using collector-local append ordinals; it is not an operating-system sequence or loss counter and cannot detect an omitted balanced load/unload pair. The protocol does not establish complete mapping history, manual or anonymous mapping absence, exact runtime closure, qualification, promotion, or Release 3 authority. Python validation remains authoritative for canonical bytes, lifecycle replay, exact checkpoint anchors, stable identity/size/read equality, token joins, digest joins, and cross-document equality.

claimBoundary.const: Windows DEBUG_PROCESS process and image events plus stable target-only K32 START/END checkpoints and borrowed debug-event file-handle identity/stable on-disk byte reads cross-checked for one R2.0 prototype execution only; handle-addressed disk bytes are not mapped or loaded memory bytes, and target checkpoint slot reconciliation uses collector-local append ordinals that cannot detect omitted balanced load/unload pairs, so this does not establish operating-system event sequences or losslessness, complete mapping history, manual or anonymous executable mapping absence, exact runtime closure, budget, qualification, promotion, or Release 3 authority.

limits.$comment: Operational collection guards only; these values are not approved R2 TCB, closure, or pack budgets.

debugger.$comment: Python validation joins every count to the event ledger and requires exact created, exited, and initial-breakpoint process sets.

events.$comment: Rows are contiguous and sequence ordered from zero. Python validation enforces NEW_PROCESS-before-EXIT_PROCESS state, exact process-set joins to the debug ledger, and a final unique ACTIVE_PROCESS_ZERO row.

job.$comment: Job Object containment and termination guards are collection mechanics, not a security sandbox or deny-by-default execution policy.

events.$comment: Rows are contiguous and sequence ordered from zero. Python validation enforces state-machine transitions, exact count joins, root-first creation, target distinction, and complete process, thread, mapping, and initial-breakpoint reconciliation.
Rows are contiguous and sequence ordered from zero with nondecreasing source-debug sequence. Python validation enforces exact load/unload lifecycle state and count reconciliation.

target_checkpoints.$comment: Exactly two target-only checkpoints. Python validation anchors START to the handled target initial breakpoint, END before target exit at the payload STOP barrier, requires two equal normalized reads per checkpoint, and replays received target image events through both local ordinals.

lossCounters.$comment: Debug wait, debug continue, and handle-close failures must be zero before evidence is emitted. K32 enumeration retry failures are disclosed as a nonnegative count; each emitted checkpoint still requires a successful stable read pair. OS/job/process/mapping loss counters and global collector/gap/unmatched counters remain exactly null. The separate collector-local append ordinal and its zero internal gap are not OS loss facts.

lossReconciliation.$comment: Python validation enforces exact process/image/checkpoint joins and target replay. target_start_end_snapshot_reconciled is target-only; broad start_end_snapshot_reconciled and event_stream_contiguous remain false, while OS and global loss counts remain null.

fileCollectionGuards.$comment: Protective collection ceilings only. They are not approved R2 budgets, closure limits, qualification inputs, or promotion authority.

fileIdentity.$comment: The volume serial and 128-bit file ID identify the handle-addressed file for this local observation. Python validation requires both values to remain equal across the before/after identity reads for the same borrowed handle.

read_passes.$comment: Python validation requires both passes to read exactly file_size_bytes bytes from offset zero through the same borrowed handle and requires their SHA-256 digests to be equal.

fileIdentityRow.$comment: Rows are contiguous and sequence ordered from zero with strictly increasing source-debug sequence. Python validation joins each row one-to-one to a CREATE_PROCESS or LOAD_DLL image event whose file_handle_present value is true.

rows.$comment: Python validation binds every non-null debug-image hFile to exactly one row, enforces stable identity/size and two equal whole-file same-handle reads, and reconciles every aggregate count and byte total.

fileIdentityTrace.$comment: This trace binds persistent FILE_ID_INFO identity and stable handle-addressed on-disk bytes for the debug-image handles surfaced by this bounded run. It explicitly does not bind mapped or loaded memory bytes, manual or anonymous executable mappings, a global mapping history, loader resolution, crypto-provider closure, or any closure/authority decision.

mappings.$comment: Rows are mapping-slot-token ordered. Python validation enforces strict ordering, unique slots, and exact equality of both normalized reads.
